stage1.impression: A clean, flat, well-built globe with a witty twist (a dish set into the North Atlantic) and a real system behind it: three size cuts with sensible switch points, and true one-colour knock-outs that hold on paper and on ink. The best form in the set is the simplest. The small cut, disc plus dish, is something you could draw from memory, and in black it reads as a Death Star at once. The colour lead is weaker than its own one-colour version. Its red-orange-yellow bullseye reads more as a target, a hotspot or a blast on the Earth than as a dish, and the emoji-style blue-and-green globe is generic. The dish crowds the coastlines on every side. In one colour its outer ring is the same tone as the land, with only hairline gaps between them, so by 32 px dish and continents fuse into white speckle. The motion is a stock radar ping. The core swells and a ring pops in at full strength by frame 02 (0.07 s): the trace jumps from near zero to its peak in two frames. The ring then sweeps the globe and fades by 0.43 s, and the figure holds about half a second before it all repeats, every second. Four pings in four seconds feels like an alert, and nothing in it says charge-and-fire. On night the ring is drawn dark, so the pulse reads as a crack rather than energy. Competent and coherent, but not yet ownable.

keep: The small cut and the one-colour build behind it: a solid disc with the driver knocked out (surround and dust cap knocked out to the ground, cone solid). It is a Death Star you can draw from memory, and it holds from 64 px down to 16 px in both black and colour (sheet 2, the colour and black small-cut rows).

The kick's skeleton: a two-frame percussive push (the rings snap concentric and the cap swells) launches one sound ring, knocked out of the globe in the ground's colour and seen only where it crosses the Earth, then comes to a clean full stop (sheet 3, frames 01-08). It is percussive and contained, and it never breaks the silhouette.

changes.problem: The dish is too big for the ocean it sits in: it presses on every North Atlantic coast and bites the land into arcs that echo its rim, so the figure reads as a target stamped on the Earth rather than a Death Star with a slightly bigger divot and Earth all round it.
changes.evidence: Sheet 1, panel 1, and sheet 2, colour full at 300 px: North America's north-east coast, Greenland's south tip and the inner edge of the Africa/Europe crescent are all cut in concave arcs that follow the dish. Sheet 3, frame 01 (t = 0.00 s): the red rim spans 51 of the globe's 134 px (0.38). I projected the card's view (-65, 12) with the lean seen on the sheet. At 24 degrees the rim already covers Newfoundland, Nova Scotia, Maine and Cape Cod, and it sits 0.004 of the radius from Cape Hatteras and 0.026 from Greenland. Lisbon, Galicia, Cape Juby and Cape Blanc sit 0.060-0.065 away, right on the LAND.clear line, so every coast in view is trimmed.
changes.expected: The dish spans about a third of the globe's width. Iberia, Morocco and West Africa clear the rim by 0.10-0.16 of the radius and keep their own coastlines, so the Africa/Europe crescent reads as land instead of a glint on the rim, and Greenland's tip just clears. Only North America's north-east, from Newfoundland down to about New York, is still trimmed; no dish position in this view avoids that. The divot is still bigger than a Death Star's, which the owner allowed, but the Earth now reads first. The small cut keeps 24 degrees (change 6).

accept.at: sheet 1, panel 1 (and t = 0.00 s on the next storyboard)
accept.check: Does the red rim span no more than 0.35 of the globe's width, with no edge of the Africa/Europe crescent following the dish's curve?

changes.problem: In one colour the dish's surround and the land are both knocked out to the ground with only 0.06 of the radius of ink between them, so at mid-cut sizes they fuse into one white shape and the driver stops reading as a driver.
changes.evidence: Sheet 2, black full and black mid at 64, 48 and 32 px: the white surround touches North America's north-east coast and the Greenland specks above the dish. At 32 px (mid cut), ring and continent merge into a single white shape. 0.06 of the radius is 1.9 px at 64 px, 1.4 px at 48 px and 1 px at 32 px, which is too little to survive anti-aliasing.
changes.what: Split LAND.clear. In the black-only and white-only versions (full and mid cuts, at every size), keep land 0.10 of the radius away from the dish's rim. The colour version keeps 0.06 from the rim, and the one-colour margin from the limb stays 0.06.
changes.parameter: LAND.clear, one-colour versions, dish rim only (new split)
changes.expected: In black and in white, an unbroken ink band at least 0.10 of the radius wide circles the surround: about 3.2 px at 64 px, 2.4 px at 48 px and 1.6 px at 32 px. The Americas and the driver read as separate shapes at every mid-cut size. The land in the colour version is unchanged, and in one colour the land still runs to within 0.06 of the limb.

accept.at: sheet 2, black mid cut at 32 px and 48 px
accept.check: At both sizes, does a continuous black gap separate the dish's white ring from North America all the way round?

changes.problem: At rest the three rings are nearly concentric bands of similar width, so the driver reads as a flat bullseye laid on the globe rather than a divot sunk into a sphere.
changes.evidence: Sheet 3, frame 01 (t = 0.00 s): along the line from the dish's centre to the globe's centre, the red band is 4 px wide on the side toward the middle and 9 px toward the limb (about 2.2 times). The cap's centre sits only 0.18 of the dish's radius off the rim's centre. At the push (frame 02, t = 0.07 s) the band is 8 px on both sides, so the depth cue at rest is small. On sheet 1, panel 1, the dish reads as three nested targets.
changes.expected: Cone and cap sit visibly toward the globe's middle, with the cap about a quarter of the dish's radius off centre. The red band thins to a lip on the inner side and widens toward the limb: a bowl seen at an angle, which is the Death Star's cue. The push to depth 0 now snaps the rings concentric with about a third more travel. This applies to the full cut only; the mid and small cuts keep 0.42 (change 6). The overshoot depth has to rise with it (change 5): left at 0.50, it would sit shallower than the new rest depth.

accept.check: Measured along the line from the dish's centre to the globe's centre, is the red band at least 2.7 times as wide on the limb side as on the side toward the middle?

changes.problem: The push barely moves the driver itself, since only the cap swells and re-centres, so the kick reads as the core blinking with a ring around it rather than a speaker cone throwing forward.
changes.evidence: Sheet 3, frames 01 to 02 (t = 0.00 to 0.07 s): the red rim grows from 51 to 53 px (about 1 px a side), while the yellow cap grows from 20 to 25 px. The driver is identical in frames 02 and 03. In the trace, the push frame (t = 0.033 s) is only 0.0038, and the peak (0.0070 at t = 0.067 s) comes mostly from the ring appearing.
changes.expected: On the push the whole driver swells by a tenth. The red rim gains 2-3 px a side at storyboard scale (about 5 px at 300 px), so the ring is seen to be thrown off a moving cone. The swell stays inside the moat left by changes 1 and 2.

accept.check: From the first frame to the second, does the red rim's width visibly grow by at least 8 %, beyond the swell of the yellow cap?

changes.problem: The return has no visible rebound, so the kick stops like a stamp instead of springing like a cone.
changes.evidence: Sheet 3, frame 05 (t = 0.27 s) compared with frame 08 (t = 0.60 s): the overshoot (depth 0.50 at 0.24 s) changes the cap by 1 px (19 against 20 px) and the dish's area by 2 % (1982 against 2022 px), which is invisible. From 0.2 s on, the trace shows only the ring fading.
changes.what: Make the overshoot a visible pull-back. At 0.24 s the dish's depth is 0.75 (the rest depth is 0.55 after change 3), the whole driver is at 0.95 of its rest size and the dust cap at 0.9. Ease (cubic in-out) from the held push at CORE.hold 0.13 s into this pull-back, then ease out to rest by CORE.rest 0.42 s. One rebound only, with no second wobble.
changes.parameter: the kick's overshoot (not a named parameter on the card)
changes.expected: Between push and rest the driver visibly sinks back once, with a smaller rim and the cap pulled deeper toward the globe's middle, then settles by 0.42 s: out, in, rest, like a woofer. The rest between beats is kept.

accept.at: t = 0.24-0.27 s, compared with t = 0.60 s
accept.check: At t = 0.24-0.27 s, is the dish visibly smaller and its yellow cap visibly further toward the globe's middle than at t = 0.60 s?

changes.problem: Changes 1 and 3 would shrink the dish and thin the inner side of its lip at the sizes where there is no land to clear and every pixel counts.
changes.evidence: Sheet 2, small cut at 16 and 24 px: at 16 px the dish is only about 6.5 px across, its bands are about 1 px wide, and in black the ring and cap only just separate. At 32 px (mid cut) the inner side of the red band is already about 1 px; depth 0.55 on a 21-degree dish would cut it to about 0.7 px.
changes.what: Size the dish optically per cut. Full cut (49 px and up): DISH.ang 21, DISH.depth 0.55. Mid cut (25-48 px): DISH.ang 21, DISH.depth 0.42. Small cut (24 px and under, no land): DISH.ang 24, DISH.depth 0.42.
changes.expected: Sizes from 16 to 48 px stay as legible as now. In black the ring and cap stay separate at 16 px, and the mid cut's lip stays about 1 px wide. Only the large sizes get the smaller, deeper divot.

accept.at: sheet 2, black small cut at 16 px
accept.check: At 16 px, do the white surround and the white dust cap still read as two separate marks?

most_important: DISH.ang from 24 to 21 degrees. A dish that fits its ocean stops biting into Iberia and West Africa and leaves Greenland clear. That gives the owner 'more earth on the outside' and turns the target into a Death Star's slightly bigger divot.
out_of_scope: Palette (fixed): the green land (#4F7F3A) on the blue ocean (#4A90C8) has only about 1.4:1 luminance contrast (relative luminance 0.17 against 0.26). The continents hold by hue alone, so they soften at 32-48 px and drop out in any greyscale reproduction of the colour version. A darker green or a lighter ocean would fix this, but the palette is fixed.
Driver colours (fixed): the red-orange-yellow steps carry a target or heat-map association that no parameter removes. More depth (change 3) is the most the card allows against it.
for_owner: What 'more earth on the outside' means. One reading is more land showing around the dish; that is the one taken here (change 1 clears Iberia and West Africa and leaves Greenland whole). The other is land reaching the globe's edge in one colour, where it is now held 0.06 off the limb. That reading would need the margin cut toward 0.03, and in black-only and white-only the land would then start to break the disc's outline.

Tempo (CORE.beat). At 1.0 s (60 BPM) the kick is a slow pulse with about 0.75 s of stillness between hits (longest_still 0.73-0.77 s): calm, close to a heartbeat. At 0.5-0.6 s (100-120 BPM) it reads as music playing, livelier but closer to busy. Whether the speakers should feel like calm hi-fi or like a party is a brand decision; the studio can show both.

The card's options that were not shown. A violet trench at the equator is the strongest Death Star cue after the dish, but it adds a line across the land, which works against 'minimal'. A violet cap at the dish's centre ties the figure to the six-colour main mark, at the cost of a fourth colour in the driver. The owner should decide whether to see them.
Legal clearance: the figure is meant to read as the Death Star, a Lucasfilm design. Get a trademark and IP check before it goes on products, especially if the trench is added.
